subject: Avalon Health — Dedicated capacity sizing and commit options
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice@avalonhealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity — sample traffic and short answers attached

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the runbook template earlier. We're starting to lock down numbers for a Dedicated commit and put together a small packet to help you size the fleet. Attached: prod_sample_traffic.csv (token-per-request samples by endpoint) and architecture-diagram.png.

Quick summary:
- Primary workload: clinical note summarization + secure chat (HIPAA scope)
- Average prompt length: 220 tokens
- Average response length: 340 tokens
- Peak concurrent sessions (observed): ~480 active sessions in a sustained 15-minute window during weekday mornings (09:00–11:00 PST)
- Burst observed: short spikes to ~1,200 concurrent sessions for ~90s when the nightly sync completes
- Typical QPS across endpoints (baseline): 18 qps; morning peak sustained: 140 qps; bursts: 360 qps
- Prefer single-region (us-west) deployment for latency and data residency

We haven't filled any formal questionnaire — can you send a short list of the exact fields you need (concurrency buckets, token distribution by endpoint, tail-latency targets, retention requirements)? We want to avoid too many back-and-forths.

Also, our procurement wants a rough monthly commit estimate + fallback/overage pricing to compare against cloud self-hosting.

Best,
Alice Zhang
Director, Platform Engineering
Avalon Health

[Attachments: prod_sample_traffic.csv (CSV, 72KB), architecture-diagram.png (PNG, 480KB)]

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@avalonhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 10:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — sample traffic and short answers attached

Thanks Alice — this is great context. Attaching our short pre-sales questionnaire (redwood_dedicated_pricing_qn.pdf) which asks for a couple of clarifications we need for a 1-2 page sizing recommendation: concurrency by API route, 95/99 latency SLO targets, percentiles for prompt/response lengths (P50/P90/P99), and expected growth over 6–12 months.

Two quick clarifications that will materially change GPU count:
1) When you say "480 active sessions" — are those long-lived chat sessions holding KV cache across requests, or mostly single-request synchronous summarization calls? If chat KV is held per-session we'll need to account for KV cache memory (and that changes optimal GPU SKU).
2) For the overnight 1,200 concurrent spike, is that a predictable ETL window we can route to a burst pool, or is it unpredictable? If it is scheduled we can propose a burst plan with short-term scaled capacity rather than a higher commit.

I'll also run a quick internal sketch and loop in Marissa for GPU SKU mix recommendations. If it's helpful, we can take 30 minutes tomorrow to walk through the CSV and align on SLOs.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_qn.pdf (PDF, 145KB)]

From: Alice Zhang <alice@avalonhealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Feb 2027 07:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — sample traffic and short answers attached

Hi Sergio,

Thanks — answers inline below and attached a small JSON snapshot (avalon_traffic_snapshot.json) that enumerates endpoints with sample token histograms.

1) Session shape: ~60% of traffic is synchronous summarization calls (one-shot), 40% are chat sessions. For the chat sessions ~70% are short interactions (<6 messages) but we do hold KV cache for the session lifetime (typical session TTL ~12 minutes). So KV footprint is non-trivial but bounded.

2) Overnight spike: it's a predictable ETL fanout that runs at 02:00 PST and fans out notifications and batch summarization jobs that cause short spikes ~90–120s. We can shift the window if needed; procurement prefers burst to be covered in commit if it's cheaper than a separate reserved pool.

Additional fields from your questionnaire (high level):
- P50 prompt: 200 tokens, P90 prompt: 420, P99 prompt: 1,200 (rare error cases)
- P50 response: 280 tokens, P90 response: 560, P99 response: 2,000
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 320ms for summarization endpoints; chat endpoints can be 95th <= 450ms
- Expected growth: 35% YoY, but targeted product rollout in Q3 could push a 3-month spike +20%

We'll join a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10:00 PST to review.

Best,
Alice

[Attachment: avalon_traffic_snapshot.json (JSON, 38KB)]

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Feb 2027 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Avalon Health — internal sizing sketch + ask

Team,

Recap from the intake + Alice's snapshot (see attachments):
- Baseline sustained peak: 140 qps with P50 prompt/response ~200/280 tokens
- Morning sustained sessions: ~480 active, chat KV TTL ~12m (40% chat)
- Predictable overnight spike: 360 qps for ~90–120s (ETL fanout)
- Latency targets: Summarization 95th <= 320ms; Chat 95th <= 450ms

My rough sizing sketch (back-of-envelope):
- Workload behavior suggests a mix of short and medium-length context; KV cache will require modest per-session memory.
- Two SKU options to propose:
  * Option A (cost-lean): 6 x A100-style GPUs (quantized mixed-precision, aggressive batching) + burst pool of 2 GPUs for ETL window. Estimated monthly commit: 160 GPU-hours/day average -> ~4800 GPU-hours/month.
  * Option B (latency-lean): 8 x H100-style GPUs (larger memory to keep more KV resident, lower tail latency) with autoscale headroom (1–2 standby GPUs). Estimated monthly commit: 220 GPU-hours/day average -> ~6600 GPU-hours/month.

Risks / open items:
- We need to validate KV memory per session sample from Alice (P99 session KV bytes) — missing from the snapshot. If KV is larger we'll push them to H100/8-sku decision.
- Confirm whether procurement prefers commit to cover predictable ETL bursts (Alice said they prefer commit if cheaper). That affects whether we include burst in the commit math or propose a separate on-demand burst pool.

Ask: Marissa, can you run a quick simulation using the avalon snapshot + our kernel efficiency assumptions and produce: (1) recommended SKU mix, (2) conservative commit estimate (monthly GPU-hours) and (3) a fallback/overage pricing line for bursts? Please leave an Excel tab with per-route QPS -> token projection and a short note rationale.

Laura — if we push Option B for latency reasons, please draft a one-paragraph justification we can include in the commercial proposal for why the higher commit reduces user-facing tail latency and improves KV cache density.

I'll include Sergio_sizing_notes.xlsx with the BE calculations and the HubSpot link in the client-facing answer once we align. Putting a 48-hour target on the internal sizing doc so we can present numbers on tomorrow's commercial review.

Thanks —
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachments referenced: sergio_sizing_notes.xlsx]
